claims.text: A machine-learning model integrating high-throughput experimental and simulation data can predict multi-step thermo-mechanical processing routes and alloy compositions.
The predicted processing routes and compositions can produce a dual-phase microstructure with a coherent dual-precipitate distribution.
The resulting microstructure can concurrently improve strength and ductility in metal alloys.
Conventional precipitation hardening and grain refinement generally exhibit a strength–ductility trade-off.
The proposed intervention is to apply an ML-predicted multi-step thermo-mechanical processing route and adjusted alloy composition.
The proposed improvement is expected under ambient-temperature, quasi-static loading.
The intervention will create multiple coherent precipitate structures combined with an optimized grain structure.
Machine-learning-guided processing optimizes the formation of fine, coherent precipitates.
Fine, coherent precipitates act as effective obstacles to dislocation motion and thereby increase strength.
The optimized precipitate structure maintains or enhances ductility by moderating stress concentrations and facilitating uniform plastic deformation.
Alloys processed using the ML-optimized route will have statistically higher yield strength than conventionally processed alloys.
Alloys processed using the ML-optimized route will have greater elongation than conventionally processed alloys.
Standard empirical thermo-mechanical treatments typically improve strength at the expense of ductility.
The approach may be limited by unrepresentative training data, scale-up challenges, extreme alloy compositions, and difficulty forming the targeted microstructure.
The model's predictive accuracy and generalization to new compositions and processing conditions remain to be validated.
